title: Adjective agreement and position
summary: Adjectives agree with the noun in gender and number: add -e for feminine, -s for plural, -es for feminine plural: un pull noir, une jupe noire, des pulls noirs, des jupes noires.

If the adjective already ends in -e, don't add another (une maison moderne), but -é still adds -e (fatiguée). If it ends in -s or -x, the masculine plural doesn't change (des garçons français, des enfants heureux).
Learn the one-offs: blanc → blanche, long → longue, gentil → gentille, frais → fraîche, gros → grosse.
Adjectives in -al have the masculine plural -aux: des problèmes sociaux (but des questions sociales).

beau, nouveau and vieux become bel, nouvel and vieil before a masculine singular noun starting with a vowel or silent h: un bel hôtel, un nouvel ami, un vieil homme. Feminine: belle, nouvelle, vieille.
marron and orange never change: des chaussures marron, une jupe orange. Two-word colours don't change either: une veste bleu foncé.

Most adjectives go after the noun: une voiture rouge, un film français. BAGS adjectives go before: Beauty (beau, joli), Age (jeune, vieux, nouveau), Good/bad (bon, mauvais), Size (grand, petit, gros): une jolie maison, un bon repas.
A few change meaning with position: mon ancien collège (my former school) / un château ancien (an old castle); un grand homme (a great man) / un homme grand (a tall man).

cards.front: What are the four forms of a regular adjective like noir?
cards.back: noir (m sg), noire (f sg), noirs (m pl), noires (f pl): un pull noir, une jupe noire, des pulls noirs, des jupes noires. The adjective agrees with the noun it describes.

cards.prompt: Ma meilleure amie est très ___ avec moi.
cards.en: My best friend is very patient with me.
cards.why: amie is feminine singular, so add -e: patiente.

cards.front: When does an adjective NOT add -e or -s?
cards.back: If it already ends in -e, it adds no extra -e: un livre rouge, une robe rouge (but -é does add -e: fatigué → fatiguée). If it ends in -s or -x, it adds no extra -s in the masculine plural: un pull gris → des pulls gris; un enfant heureux → des enfants heureux.

cards.en: My little sisters are quite shy.
cards.why: timide already ends in -e, so the feminine plural just adds -s: timides.

cards.front: How do adjectives ending in -eux, -if, -er, -on, -el and -ien form the feminine?
cards.back: -eux → -euse (heureux → heureuse), -if → -ive (sportif → sportive), -er → -ère (cher → chère), -on → -onne (bon → bonne), -el → -elle (naturel → naturelle), -ien → -ienne (canadien → canadienne).

cards.prompt: Ma grand-mère est toujours ___ quand nous lui rendons visite.
cards.en: My grandmother is always happy when we visit her.

cards.prompt: Ma tante est très ___ : elle fait du vélo tous les jours.
cards.en: My aunt is very sporty: she goes cycling every day.

cards.prompt: Au marché, les fraises sont trop ___ en ce moment.
cards.en: At the market, strawberries are too expensive at the moment.
cards.why: fraises is feminine plural: -er becomes -ère, then add -s: chères.

cards.prompt: Cette tarte aux pommes est vraiment ___ !
cards.en: This apple tart is really good!
cards.why: -on doubles the n and adds -e in the feminine: bonne.
-el doubles the l and adds -e in the feminine: traditionnelle.

cards.front: Give the feminine of blanc, long, gentil, frais and gros – and the masculine plural of social.
cards.back: blanche, longue, gentille, fraîche, grosse. Adjectives in -al have the masculine plural -aux: social → sociaux (but the feminine plural is regular: sociales).

cards.prompt: Mes grands-parents habitent dans une maison ___ au bord de la mer.
cards.en: My grandparents live in a white house by the sea.
cards.why: blanc has an irregular feminine: blanche.

cards.prompt: Au lycée, nous parlons souvent des problèmes ___.
cards.en: At school we often talk about social problems.
cards.why: problèmes is masculine plural, and adjectives in -al change to -aux: sociaux.

cards.front: Give all the forms of beau, nouveau and vieux.
cards.back: beau, bel, belle, beaux, belles; nouveau, nouvel, nouvelle, nouveaux, nouvelles; vieux, vieil, vieille, vieux, vieilles. bel, nouvel and vieil are used only before a masculine singular noun starting with a vowel or silent h: un bel endroit, un nouvel ordinateur, un vieil ami.

cards.prompt: Nous habitons dans un ___ appartement au centre-ville.
cards.en: We live in a beautiful flat in the town centre.
cards.why: Before a masculine singular noun starting with a vowel or silent h, beau becomes bel.

cards.prompt: Le ___ hôtel près de la gare est très moderne.
cards.en: The new hotel near the station is very modern.
cards.why: hôtel is masculine and starts with a silent h, so nouveau becomes nouvel.

cards.prompt: Un ___ homme m'a demandé le chemin de la gare.
cards.en: An old man asked me the way to the station.
cards.why: homme is masculine and starts with a silent h, so vieux becomes vieil.

cards.prompt: Les plages de cette région sont très ___.
cards.en: The beaches in this region are very beautiful.
cards.why: plages is feminine plural: belle + s = belles.

cards.back: marron and orange (they are also nouns – a chestnut, an orange): des yeux marron, des chaussettes orange. Two-word colours don't change either: une robe bleu clair. Other colours agree as normal: une veste verte, des baskets blanches.

cards.prompt: Pour la fête, Julie porte des chaussures ___.
cards.en: For the party, Julie is wearing brown shoes.
cards.why: marron (like orange) is invariable: it never adds -e or -s.

cards.front: Most adjectives go after the noun. Which ones go before? (BAGS)
cards.back: Beauty: beau, joli. Age: jeune, vieux, nouveau. Good/bad: bon, mauvais. Size: grand, petit, gros. E.g. une jolie ville, un vieux pont, un bon film, une grande maison. Colours and nationalities always go after: un vélo bleu, une voiture allemande.

cards.instruction: Add both adjectives in brackets, in the correct form and their usual position (without et).
answers: Nous avons une petite voiture rouge.
cards.en: We have a small red car.
cards.why: petit is a BAGS (size) adjective, so it goes before the noun; colours go after. Both agree with voiture (f): petite, rouge.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence about Marie instead of Marc.
cards.why: In the feminine, -if becomes -ive and -eux becomes -euse.

cards.front: How does position change the meaning of ancien, cher and grand?
cards.back: Before the noun: mon ancien collège (my former school), mes chers amis (my dear friends), un grand homme (a great man). After the noun: une maison ancienne (an old house), un hôtel cher (an expensive hotel), un homme grand (a tall man).
